harvests.note: The shape that an ERP document's meaningful, billable events are its CREATION and its STATE TRANSITIONS (draft -> submitted -> completed, with a cancel path), not its edits or reads. Harvested as a shape only: this lane declares its own operation vocabulary (create/transition), its own event names and its own rate card, and reproduces none of ERPNEXT's doctype definitions, hooks or Python.

In-repo harvest, credited with the same record the doctrine requires for an upstream one. From integrations/paperclip/budget.py this lane took the SHAPE that a metering record, a charge derived from a declared rail, and a hard stop derived from a cap percentage are three separate facts with three separate names - not its code. The ERP lane derives its stop from the platform budget ladder instead of from a cap percentage of a single charge.

In-repo harvest. The ladder (allow / warn / would_warn / would_block / block), the soft-vs-hard cap distinction and the observe-vs-enforce mode are CONSUMED from telemetry.budgets as the public API they are - this lane constructs TenantBudgetPolicy objects and calls BudgetEnforcer rather than re-implementing the ladder. The harvest recorded here is the shape of the decision object, which is what made a named refusal (budget-exhausted) expressible over it.

In-repo harvest. From telemetry/ledger this lane took the shape that an append-only record carries (tenant, actor, action, resource, evidence, ts) and the tri-state verification discipline (OK / NOT-OK / CANNOT-ASSESS). It is CONSUMED through the public API (open_ledger, LedgerStore.append, verify_ledger) and never edited: acceptance criterion 3 of issue #654 is exactly that this lane owns no copy of the ledger's files.
